topic.angle: The loop a CPU repeats from boot-up to shutdown

panels.text: Under all the apps, a CPU does one thing over and over: the instruction cycle. It runs from boot-up until the computer shuts down.
Fetch. A register called the program counter holds the address of the next instruction. The CPU reads that instruction from memory, and the counter moves on to the one after.
Decode. The control unit works out what the instruction means: which operations and operands are needed, and it signals the parts of the CPU that will do the work.
Execute. The CPU carries it out. Then the cycle starts again with the next instruction.

probes.question: What is the right order of the instruction cycle?
True or false: the CPU follows the fetch-decode-execute cycle from boot-up until the computer shuts down.

claims.claim: The CPU follows the instruction cycle from boot-up until shutdown
claims.quote: the cycle that the central processing unit (CPU) follows from boot-up until the computer has shut down
It is composed of three main stages: the fetch stage, the decode stage, and the execute stage.

claims.claim: Fetch: program counter holds address of next instruction
claims.quote: The PC contains the address of the instruction to be fetched.

claims.claim: Fetch: counter then moves on to the following instruction
claims.quote: At the end of this stage, the PC points to the next instruction that will be read at the next cycle.

claims.claim: Decode: control unit interprets the instruction and signals the CPU parts that do the work
claims.quote: the encoded instruction in the CIR is interpreted by the CU.

claims.claim: Execute: the CPU carries out the operation
claims.quote: This is the stage where the actual operation specified by the instruction is carried out by the relevant functional units of the CPU.
